contribution: The authors analysed ==1,169 spontaneous questions== about biology and physics sent to online and TV science services.
Biology made up 53.8% of females’ questions and 38.3% of males’; physics, 6% versus 13.2%.
The gap ==widened with age==, as girls seemed to develop less interest in physics than boys did.
today: Studying the questions learners ==chose to ask themselves== remains a fresh alternative to rating predefined topics.
Nearly two decades on, it invites reflection on how experiences ==inside and outside school== shape disciplinary interests.
Could students’ spontaneous questions help ==make physics more inclusive== without reinforcing stereotypes?
